post.summary: Record a relationship between two residents
post.description: Needs family.manage. Resident to resident, so it survives either person moving; stored in one canonical direction (see RelationshipKind). Both people must be on file and in the writer's scope: the resident in the path answers 404 when not, the other person 409 resident-not-found. An own-barangay account works in its barangay; an assigned-cases account is 403, as on the resident registry. The same link already standing (either way round for spouse-of and sibling-of) answers 200 with the standing relationship and records nothing, so a retried request never records a second marriage. Otherwise 201: relationship-recorded is appended to office_family_events with the reason, and audit office_relationship.recorded. A parent-of that reverses a parent link already on file is 409 contradicts-existing.

get.description: Needs household.view. An address and who lives there, recorded by staff — not the residents' app households (/api/v1/households); nothing is shared between the two. By reference number. An own-barangay account sees only its barangay; an assigned-cases account may ask only resident_id, for one of its own clients, and is answered with that household or an empty page; anything else is 403 (DL-183). q matches every word (up to five) against the reference number, the head's surname and the street address, but not the street address of a protected household for a reader without request.view-sensitive. resident_id answers which household a person is in. minimum_band filters on the advisory band; to fill such a page up to 500 rows are read per request, so a short page can still say has_more. head is the resident registry's redacted record. band is the same for every role, computed from the unredacted records; present_factor_count counts the factors present as this reader is shown them. Nothing here decides eligibility. Every member of a household with a protected member, or of a family with one or living in a household that has one, also has street_address and purok_or_sitio withheld from that reader (withheld names exact_address): people who share a record usually share a roof, and a member's address listed beside the masked one would say where the protected person lives.

get.description: Needs household.view. The household, its current members (head first, then in the order they joined) as the resident registry's redacted records, its vulnerability snapshot, and its events newest first. Out of scope answers 404, exactly as one that does not exist. A social worker (assigned-cases) reads the household one of their own clients lives in — the subject of a filed request or a case assigned to them — and for nobody else (404, as absent) (DL-183). A household with a member under vawc-survivor or cicl (is_protected) withholds street_address and purok_or_sitio from a reader without request.view-sensitive (withheld: ["exact_address"]), because that address is where the protected person lives. For that reader the protected-member factor reads withheld, with an empty basis, origin computed and no correction, and its correction events are left out; likewise the two income factors for a reader without resident.view-sensitive; the band is not recomputed, so every role reads the same band. Every member of a household with a protected member, or of a family with one or living in a household that has one, also has street_address and purok_or_sitio withheld from that reader (withheld names exact_address): people who share a record usually share a roof, and a member's address listed beside the masked one would say where the protected person lives.

post.summary: Change who lives in a household
post.description: Needs household.manage. The head is removed only when the same change names another. A person joins only if on file, in the writer's scope (otherwise member-not-found) and in no other household. One reason for the whole change; one event per intent in office_household_events, each with that reason; audit office_household.membership_changed.

get.description: Needs family.view. A family is a claim about who belongs to whom, not an address: it names its members and points at the household it lives in, or at none while between addresses. By reference number; dissolved families only with include_dissolved=true. An own-barangay account sees a family whose household is in its barangay, or — with no household — one whose every current member is recorded as living there; an assigned-cases account is 403. q matches every word (up to five) against the reference number, the family's name and the current head's surname. barangay_id is the household's barangay, so it leaves out families with no household. Out of one family and into another as one act, so nobody is dropped from every family on file halfway. from_family_id null joins a family; to_family_id null leaves one; never both. The person and each family named must be on file and in the writer's scope (otherwise resident-not-found or family-not-found). Leaving closes the person's membership period (left_on); joining opens a new one with role. With move_household and a destination family that has a household, the person also moves out of their current household and into that one as a relative, recorded there as member-removed and member-added with the same reason. The reason is at least 8 characters. A transfer that has already landed answers 200 and records nothing. Appends resident-transferred to office_family_events; audit office_family.transferred, against the resident. Answers the destination family, or the family left when there is none.

post.summary: Start or continue a thread with an office
post.description: Verified residents only. subject is stored when the thread is created. An open thread for the same resident and office is reused and keeps its original subject. A closed thread starts a new one. An optional idempotency_key (a UUID, in the body; a multipart field with a file) makes a retry safe: the same key with the same office, subject, words and image answers with the message the first send made and the thread as it stands, with the status the first send had (201 when that message opened the thread, 200 otherwise), before anything else is read or stored and without telling the office again. Keys are kept per sender in message_intents (0040), append-only. A send with no key behaves as before.

An optional idempotency_key (a UUID, in the body; a multipart field with a file): the same key with the same thread, words and image answers 201 with the message the first send made and the thread as it stands — even after the thread was closed — before anything else is stored, and without telling anybody again. A send with no key behaves as before.
